A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SynerMedGen work. All pages, including Appendices A-E, are readable, and corresponding equations, tables, figures, and renumbered appendix content can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthesis and understanding evaluations, component ablations, and generalization experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds standard medical VQA evaluations, additional task ablations, and downstream brain tumor segmentation results.

M1.justification: The Bagel-based architecture, CTS/MI/TIA tasks, objectives, and two-stage GAU/UCG procedure are unchanged. The added nnU-Net experiment evaluates generated images downstream; it does not modify SynerMedGen.

E1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds evaluation on VQA-RAD, SLAKE, OmniMedVQA, and MMMU-Med, extending understanding evaluation beyond the constructed generation-aligned tasks. Appendix B.4 adds brain tumor segmentation on the already-used BraTS dataset. Existing synthesis and generalization coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Table 9 introduces InternVL2 as an evaluated comparator alongside Bagel and HealthGPT. Existing synthesis and generation-aligned understanding comparator sets remain unchanged. Figure 15 adds qualitative comparisons with Pix2Pix, BBDM, and SynDiff, which were already quantitative baselines.

E3.justification: The new segmentation evaluation specifies 100 BraTS cases, a 70/10/20 train/validation/test split, nnU-Net, DSC, and three input conditions. Additional task combinations are evaluated after Stage I and Stage I+II. The new volume-level synthesis evaluation description discloses previously unspecified settings without establishing that existing experiments changed or were rerun.

E4.justification: v1's progressive CTS-to-CTS+MI-to-full ablation is supplemented by all individual and paired task combinations at both training stages in Table 10. Table 11 tests whether synthetic T1CE helps tumor segmentation, and Figure 15 adds qualitative comparisons with dedicated synthesis methods. The existing K-sensitivity and generalization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Existing plotted error bars are retained. No run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical tests are added; new Tables 9-11 report point estimates.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1-8 and the K-sensitivity results are unchanged. New results include VQA-RAD scores of 61.3 for SynerMedGen versus 60.1 for Bagel, MI-only ablation SSIM of 50.72/83.34 after Stage I/Stage I+II, and segmentation DSC of 56.25 without T1CE, 62.48 with synthetic T1CE, and 64.83 with real T1CE. Figure 15 adds qualitative synthesis outputs.

T1.justification: The mathematical task definitions and loss equations (1)-(6) are unchanged. No theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central contributions: generation-aligned understanding through three tasks, two-stage transfer to synthesis, strong results across 22 synthesis tasks, and the SynerMed release. The new evaluations support these contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new VQA results as preserving general medical understanding and potentially improving fine-grained representations, and the segmentation results as evidence of useful tumor-related cues. The conclusion explicitly identifies the current framework's 2D scope and proposes 3D volumetric modeling as future work.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly documents slice-wise inference, reconstruction of volumes in original slice order, and volume-level metric computation for all methods. The project link changes from Mhilab/SynerMedGen to piooip/SynerMedGen; the PDFs do not establish whether resource availability changed.

R1.justification: The related-work sections and reference list are unchanged, as is the positioning around misalignment between medical understanding and generation. New benchmarking does not revise the claimed novelty or relationship to prior approaches.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited abstract and conclusion edits, adds an evaluation-protocol paragraph and appendix subsections, removes an unresolved reference marker, and adds acknowledgements and conference publication text. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds three compact result tables and Figure 15 with magnified qualitative comparisons, plus running headers and local layout changes. Existing displays are retained: v1 Table 9 becomes Table 12, and appendix example Figures 15-27 become Figures 16-28.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the central understanding-generation premise. Compared with v1's task-aligned understanding tests and progressive ablation, Tables 9-10 provide external VQA checks and isolate individual and paired task contributions. Table 11 adds downstream evidence of tumor-relevant usefulness beyond image-fidelity scores and visual inspection. These address important evidential gaps, while the volume-level evaluation description and explicit 2D limitation improve interpretability. New experiment settings remain sparsely documented and uncertainty reporting is still limited, but the overall evidential gains are substantial.
